newsitem.title: UK: Toyota confident in UK, Major says.
newsitem.headline: Toyota confident in UK, Major says.

text.p: The British government reacted quickly on Wednesday after Toyota's president appeared to rule out new investments in Britain and warned investment could shift to Europe if London stays out of Europe's single currency.
A spokesman for Prime Minister John Major's Downing Street office said: "I am not going to take it at face value."
But he said an announcement last year that Toyota would create around 1,000 jobs through an additional 200 million sterling investment to boost capacity at its Derbyshire plant.
"That indicates to me great confidence in the United Kingdom," the spokesman said.
Saying that figures showed Britain was still the leading destination for inward investment into Europe, he added: "The United Kingdom is the place to be and will remain so."
Toyota chairman Hiroshi Okuda said the Japanese carmaker was already reviewing its levels of investment in Britain.
"Regardless on whether Britain joins (the EMU), I have a feeling that it would be excessive if we made additional (investments) in Britain," Okuda told reporters in Tokyo.
But Okuda said Toyota would shift its European investments to continental Europe if Britain did not join the EMU. -- London Newsroom +44-171-542-7768
